After her young son died and her husband the raja passed, she took up the leadership of her princely state and fought battle after battle against the British in the Indian Rebellion of 1857. Who is she?
Rani of Jhansi: Prominent leader of the 1857 Indian rebellion.
A U.S. attorney general turned New York senator, this icon of American liberalism was assassinated in 1968 — and his brothers John and Ted were no strangers to office either. Who is he?
Robert F. Kennedy: American politician and lawyer (1925–1968)
A career diplomat turned politician, this BJP member rose from foreign secretary to become India's longest-serving minister to hold the External Affairs portfolio exclusively. Who is he?
S. Jaishankar: Indian diplomat and politician (born 1955)
Dominating the Pontic steppe from the 5th century BC to the 4th century AD, this confederation of ancient Iranian horse nomads formed part of the wider Scythian world — who were they?
Sarmatians: Large Iranian confederation that existed in classical antiquity.

Spurned in childhood as an illegitimate son, this early-19th-century monarch transformed his kingdom's army into a formidable fighting force during his reign from 1816 to 1828 — who was this Southern African king?
Shaka: Zulu king from 1816 to 1828. King Shaka was born in the lunar month of uNtulikazi (July) in 1787, in Mthonjaneni, KwaZulu-Natal Province, South Africa.
Stepping up from hostess for her assassinated husband, this Sri Lankan politician became, in 1960, the first woman in the world elected prime minister — who was she?
Sirimavo Bandaranaike: Prime Minister of Sri Lanka (1916–2000)
Released from Dutch detention by invading Japanese forces in WWII, this nationalist leader went on to become the very first president of his newly independent nation. Who is he?
Sukarno: President of Indonesia from 1945 to 1967.
This brief conflict ran from June 27 to July 7, 1991, ending when the Brioni Accords settled Slovenia's break from Yugoslavia — what was it called?

Ten-Day War: 1991 Slovenia-Yugoslavia conflict. It was fought between the Slovenian Territorial Defence and the Slovenian National Police Force on one side, and the Yugoslav People's Army on the other.
Before ruling Rome from 79 to 81 AD, he commanded the siege that ended the Jewish rebellion — and became the first Roman emperor ever to directly succeed his own biological father; who was he?
Titus: Roman emperor from AD 79 to 81. Titus Flavius Vespasianus (30 December 39 – 13 September 81 AD) was Roman emperor from 79 to 81 AD.

Centered on the Armenian highlands between three great lakes and locked in frequent wars with Assyria, this Iron Age kingdom left behind cuneiform inscriptions and massive fortresses before falling to the Medes or Cyrus the Great — what kingdom was it?
Urartu: Iron-Age kingdom of the ancient Near East.
Leading Russia's Liberal Democratic Party from 1992 until his death in 2022, this firebrand ran in nearly every presidential election and openly called for military action against NATO — who is he?
Once a loyal Nazi admiral running Germany's military intelligence service, he turned to sabotage and resistance against Hitler — and was hanged for treason at Flossenbürg in 1945. Who was he?

After his father — a former Andhra Pradesh chief minister — died in a 2009 helicopter crash, this politician toured the state on a consoling 'Odarpu Yatra' before founding his own party and later becoming chief minister himself — who is he?

Y. S. Jagan Mohan Reddy: Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh, India. Jagan Mohan Reddy started his political career in the Indian National Congress and was elected as the Member of Parliament of Kadapa in 2009.
Pakistan's longest-serving de-facto ruler, this general seized power in a 1977 coup and held it until his death in a 1988 airplane crash — who is he?
Zia-ul-Haq: 6th President of Pakistan from 1978 to 1988.
Who among these was born first?
Omar Khayyam (born 1048) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these people was born first?
Saint Valentine (born 175) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four came first?
Assembly language (founded 1949) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these was founded earliest?
Pascal (programming language) (founded 1970) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is a physicist?
Who among these is a chemist?
Dmitri Mendeleev is a chemist. The synthetic element mendelevium is named in his honor.
What is the atomic number of Flerovium?
Flerovium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Fl and atomic number 114.
What is the atomic number of Yttrium?
Yttrium is a chemical element; it has symbol Y and atomic number 39.
In what year was Galileo Galilei born?
Galileo Galilei: Galileo has been called the father of observational astronomy, modern-era classical physics, the scientific method, and modern science.
In what year was Anton Chekhov born?
Anton Chekhov: Along with Henrik Ibsen and August Strindberg, Chekhov is often referred to as one of the three seminal figures in the birth of early modernism in the theatre.
In what year was Max Weber born?
Max Weber: Born in Erfurt in 1864, Weber studied law and history in Berlin, Göttingen, and Heidelberg.
In what year did Gregor Mendel die?
Gregor Mendel: Mendel worked with seven characteristics of pea plants: plant height, pod shape and colour, seed shape and colour, and flower position and colour.
In what year did Adam Smith die?
Adam Smith: The work is notable for its contribution to economic theory, particularly in its exposition of the concept of absolute advantage.
In what year was Argon discovered?
Argon is a chemical element; it has symbol Ar and atomic number 18.
Which company manufactures Consolidated B-24 Liberator?
Lockheed Martin Missiles and Fire Control
Consolidated B-24 Liberator: North American Aviation. The Consolidated B-24 Liberator is an American heavy bomber, designed by Consolidated Aircraft of San Diego, California.
Cro-Magnon: France. Cro-Magnons produced Upper Palaeolithic cultures, the first major one being the Aurignacian, which was succeeded by the Gravettian by 30,000 years ago.
Who is credited with discovering Circinus?
Circinus: Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. Circinus is a small, faint constellation in the southern sky, first defined in 1756 by the French astronomer Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille.
Who is credited with discovering Citric acid?
Citric acid: Carl Wilhelm Scheele. Citric acid is an organic compound with the formula C6H8O7.
Who is credited with discovering Helium?
Helium: Pierre Janssen. Helium (from Ancient Greek: ἥλιος, romanized: helios, lit. 'sun') is a chemical element; it has symbol He and atomic number 2.
Russell Crowe stars in this 2001 Ron Howard film about a Nobel Prize-winning mathematician's struggle with schizophrenia, based on Sylvia Nasar's biography. What's the title?
A Beautiful Mind (film) is a 2001 American biographical drama film about the mathematician John Nash who won a Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences.
This French surgeon won the 1912 Nobel for pioneering vascular suturing, then teamed up with aviator Charles Lindbergh to build the first perfusion pump for organ transplantation. Who was he?
Alexis Carrel (28 June 1873 - 5 November 1944) was a French surgeon and biologist who spent most of his scientific career in the United States.
Dating back to the Neolithic Revolution around 13,000 BC, this branch of agriculture covers the breeding, feeding, and day-to-day care of livestock raised for meat, milk, or fiber — what's it called?
Animal husbandry is the branch of agriculture concerned with animals that are raised for meat, fibre, milk, or other products.
This American physicist won a share of the 1927 Nobel Prize for an effect, now bearing his name, that demonstrated light's particle nature — who was he?
Arthur Compton (September 10, 1892 - March 15, 1962) was an American physicist who shared the 1927 Nobel Prize in Physics with C. T. R. Wilson.
Grown for its edible taproot in red or golden varieties and closely related to Swiss chard, this vegetable's leaves are eaten too, sold simply as "greens" — which root vegetable?
Beetroot is the taproot portion of a Beta vulgaris subsp.
Born as Hughes Helicopters' Model 77 to replace the AH-1 Cobra, this twin-turboshaft attack helicopter packs a 30 mm chain gun and Hellfire missiles in a tandem cockpit — what is it?
Boeing AH-64 Apache (-) is an American twin-turboshaft attack helicopter with a tailwheel-type landing gear and a tandem cockpit for a crew of two.
This basic unit of digital information most often consists of eight bits, and is called an 'octet' in network protocol documents to avoid ambiguity. What is it?
Byte is a unit of digital information that most commonly consists of eight bits.
Combining science, aesthetics, and technique, this field is the study and practice of making and using maps to communicate spatial information — what field is it?

Cartography is the study and practice of making and using maps. The fundamental objectives of traditional cartography are to:

Set the map's agenda and select traits of the object to be mapped.
Besides identifying the laws of elastic collision, this Dutch polymath studied Saturn's rings and improved the design of the telescope — who is he?
Christiaan Huygens (14 April 1629 - 8 July 1695) was a Dutch mathematician, physicist, engineer, astronomer, and inventor who is regarded as a key figure in the Scientific Revolution.
Scholars still argue whether it merely transmits meaning or also creates it, but the simplest definition of this concept is the transmission of information — what is it?
Communication is commonly defined as the transmission of information.
Grown from tubers and known by the folk name 'sowbread,' this Primulaceae genus features flowers with distinctively upswept petals — which plant genus?
Cyclamen is a genus of 25 species of perennial flowering plants in the family Primulaceae.
This Russian chemist's great law let him predict three undiscovered elements — germanium, gallium, and scandium — and a synthetic element now bears his name; who was he?
Which American toy magnate teamed up with his wife Ruth to co-found Mattel and dream up Hot Wheels and Barbie?
Elliot Handler (April 9, 1916 - July 21, 2011) was an American inventor, business magnate, and the co-founder of Mattel.
Botanists use this word for any plant whose leaves stay green and functional through every season, never going bare like a deciduous tree — what is it?
Evergreen is a plant which has foliage that remains green and functional throughout the year.
Holding doctorates in both medicine and philosophy from Pisa by age 21, this Italian naturalist became the "founder of experimental biology" by disproving spontaneous generation — who was he?
Francesco Redi (18 February 1626 - 1 March 1697) was an Italian physician, naturalist, biologist, and poet.
The tallest living land animal and the largest ruminant on Earth, this African mammal's closest living relative is the shorter-necked okapi — name the animal?
Giraffe (genus Giraffa) are large African hoofed mammals.
This flatfish's English name blends words for 'holy' and 'flat fish,' a nod to its place on the Catholic holy-day menu. Which bottom-dwelling fish?
Halibut is the common name for three species of flatfish in the family of right-eye flounders.
Nesting monogamously in tree cavities across Africa, Asia, and Melanesia, these birds are unique for having their first two neck vertebrae fused solid — which birds?
Hornbill are birds found in tropical and subtropical Africa, Asia and Melanesia of the family Bucerotidae.
Supplied by the lumbar spinal nerves and part of the femoral nerve, this fused pair of abdominal and thigh muscles is the body's strongest hip flexor — what is it called?
Iliopsoas (from Latin ile 'groin' and Ancient Greek (ps) 'muscles of the loins') refers to the joined psoas major and the iliacus muscles.
This condition causes a yellowish, sometimes greenish, tint to the skin and eyes due to high bilirubin levels, affecting an estimated 80% of babies in their first week of life — what is it called?
Jaundice is a yellowish or, less frequently, greenish pigmentation of the skin and sclera due to high bilirubin levels.

This American game show host and former software engineer won 74 consecutive games on a legendary quiz show in 2004, the longest streak in its history, before becoming its host himself in 2021 — who is he?
Ken Jennings (born May 23, 1974) is an American game show host and author who has hosted the syndicated quiz show Jeopardy!
This Swiss polymath founded the study of graph theory and topology, and introduced much of modern mathematical notation, including the concept of a function — who is he?
Leonhard Euler (15 April 1707 - 18 September 1783) was a Swiss polymath who was active as a mathematician, physicist, astronomer, logician, geographer, music theorist and engineer.
Native to Afghanistan and Iran but long grown in Europe, this herb's leaves, roots, and seeds are all used in cooking, tasting like a more intense mix of celery and parsley — what is it?
Lovage (Levisticum officinale) is a perennial plant, the sole species in the genus Levisticum in the family Apiaceae, subfamily Apioideae.
Cold-sensitive and tasting of sweet pine and citrus, this kitchen herb is so close to its cousin that in parts of the Middle East the two names are used interchangeably with oregano. What is it?
Connecting the diencephalon and cerebrum to the pons, this brainstem structure plays a role in vision, hearing, and staying alert -- what is it called?
Midbrain is the uppermost portion of the brainstem connecting the diencephalon and cerebrum with the pons.
This semiaquatic rodent can stay submerged for up to seventeen minutes, propelled mainly by its webbed hind feet while its long, scaly tail helps steer — what animal is it?
Muskrat (Ondatra zibethicus) is a medium-sized semiaquatic rodent.
First isolated by Scottish physician Daniel Rutherford, which group-15 nonmetal with atomic number 7 is the most abundant species in Earth's atmosphere?
Nitrogen is a chemical element; it has symbol N and atomic number 7.
Usually caused by bacteria and sometimes requiring amputation in severe cases, this infectious inflammation of bone can be acute or chronic — which condition?
Osteomyelitis (OM) is the infectious inflammation of bone. It may be acute or chronic and can be classified as hematogenous or non-hematogenous.

Also known as underage medicine, this branch of medicine covers care from infancy through adolescence — typically up to age 18 in most of the Commonwealth, but only 12 in India. Name the medical specialty?

Pediatrics (American English), also spelled paediatrics (British English) and also known as underage medicine, is the branch of medicine that involves the medical care of infants, toddlers, children, adolescents, and young adults.
Confirming and popularizing Isaac Newton's work, this French scholar authored the five-volume 'Mécanique céleste' and helped pioneer the Bayesian view of probability — who is he?

Pierre-Simon Laplace (23 March 1749 - 5 March 1827) was a French polymath, a scholar whose work has been instrumental in the fields of physics, astronomy, mathematics, engineering, statistics, and philosophy.
This chemical compound, known in nature as the mineral niter and historically as a form of saltpetre, is widely used in fertilizers. What is it?
Potassium nitrate is a chemical compound with a sharp, salty, bitter taste and the chemical formula KNO3.
Powered by a supermassive black hole accreting gas at its center, this extremely luminous type of galactic nucleus can outshine an entire galaxy thousands of times over. What is it?
Quasar is an extremely luminous active galactic nucleus (AGN).

Winner of the 1905 Nobel Prize for his work on tuberculosis, this German physician identified the causative agents of tuberculosis, cholera, and anthrax, earning him the nickname 'father of microbiology' alongside Louis Pasteur — name this scientist?
Robert Koch (KOKH; 11 December 1843 - 27 May 1910) was a German physician and microbiologist.
This systematic discipline builds testable explanations about nature and society, and is continuously challenged and validated by the community that practices it. What is it?
Science is a systematic discipline that builds and organises knowledge in the form of testable explanations about nature and society.
Long, thin and transparent, this hydrozoan drifts through the ocean as a colony of specialized zooids that together handle feeding, floating and jet propulsion — what marine organism is this?
Siphonophore (from Ancient Greek (siphn), meaning "tube" and - (-phros), meaning "bearing") are cnidarian animals of the hydrozoan order Siphonophorae.
Haunted by the Holocaust and the Eichmann trial, this American social psychologist ran his notorious obedience experiments in a Yale basement in 1961. Who was he?
Stanley Milgram (August 15, 1933 - December 20, 1984) was an American social psychologist who conducted controversial experiments on obedience in the 1960s during his professorship at Yale.
Deriving its name from a French word for crushed oak bark used in hide-curing, this class of astringent plant compounds binds to and precipitates proteins and other organic molecules — what is it?
Tannin (or tannoids) are a class of astringent, polyphenolic biomolecules that bind to and precipitate proteins and various other organic compounds including amino acids and alkaloids.
Shaped like a butterfly and located in the neck just below the Adam's apple, this endocrine gland's two lobes are joined by a thin band of tissue called the isthmus — name the gland?

Thyroid is an endocrine gland in vertebrates. The lower two thirds of the lobes are connected by a thin band of tissue called the isthmus (pl.: isthmi). The thyroid gland secretes three hormones: the two thyroid hormones – triiodothyronine (T3) and thyroxine (T4) – and a peptide hormone, calcitonin.
This break in the skin or mucous membrane involves tissue breakdown severe enough to expose the dermis or fat beneath, and often becomes infected with pus — what condition is it?
Ulcer (dermatology) is a sore on the skin or a mucous membrane, accompanied by the disintegration of tissue.
This slender, short-legged predator's genus also includes polecats, stoats, and ferrets, and its smallest species is the tiniest carnivore on Earth — what animal is it?
Weasel are mammals of the genus Mustela of the family Mustelidae.
Earning his doctorate in Islamic philosophy at George Washington University under Seyyed Hossein Nasr, this Turkish academic now directs the country's National Intelligence Organization — who is he?
İbrahim Kalın (born 15 September 1971) is a Turkish bureaucrat and academic who is the current director of the National Intelligence Organization (MT).
Considered sacred by Hindus and Buddhists, this tree native to the Indian subcontinent is also known as bael and is the sole member of its genus — which species?
Aegle marmelos: Species of tree, considered sacred by Hindus. It is present in India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, and Nepal as a naturalized species.

An anatomist and archaeologist turned TV presenter, she has served as professor of Public Engagement in Science at the University of Birmingham since 2012 and once led the charity Humanists UK — who is she?
Alice Roberts: English academic, TV presenter and author.
Nominated by Donald Trump in 2020, this Notre Dame law professor became the fifth woman to serve as a US Supreme Court associate justice after previously sitting on the Seventh Circuit — who is she?

Amy Coney Barrett: US Supreme Court justice since 2020. Barrett graduated from Rhodes College before attending Notre Dame Law School, earning a Juris Doctor (J.D.) degree in 1997 and ranked first in her class.
Who is this — “American-Yemeni Islamic cleric and lecturer (1971–2011)”?
Anwar al-Awlaki: American-Yemeni Islamic cleric and lecturer (1971–2011). Al-Awlaki was the first U.S. citizen to be targeted and assassinated by a U.S. government drone strike.

Also known by a folksy nickname, this small North American tree produces a custard-textured fruit tasting like banana or pineapple — despite containing a neurotoxin elsewhere in the plant. What species is it?
Asimina triloba: Species of tree. Asimina triloba, the American papaw, pawpaw, paw paw, or paw-paw, among many regional names, is a species of small deciduous tree.
This fig tree spreads outward indefinitely by growing extra trunks from its own prop roots, and its most famous species is the national tree of India — what is it?
Both heads of this upper-arm muscle originate on the scapula and let you flex your elbow while turning your palm upward — what muscle is it?

Biceps: Muscle on the front of the upper arm. While the long head of the biceps crosses both the shoulder and elbow joints, its main function is at the elbow where it flexes and supinates the forearm.

Flying for the U.S. Air Force since 1955, this subsonic strategic bomber evolved from a six-turboprop straight-wing design into eight swept-wing turbojets and can haul up to 70,000 pounds of weapons — what's its name?
Boeing B-52 Stratofortress: American strategic bomber aircraft.

This Italian-American physicist invented an improved coincidence circuit and traveled to Eritrea to prove cosmic rays arrive more strongly from the West than the East, before Italy's racial laws forced him to flee — who was he?
Which multidrug-resistant fungal yeast colonizes skin in long-term care facilities and causes bloodstream infections with up to a 60% mortality rate?
Also known by the nickname 'catawba,' this genus of flowering trees is native to warm regions of North America, the Caribbean, and East Asia — what genus is it?
Native to the mountains of Honduras and Guatemala and nicknamed the 'custard apple' for its creamy texture, this fruit was called 'the most delicious fruit known to men' by Mark Twain — which fruit?
Cherimoya: Edible fruit-bearing species of plant.
What is this — “Physiological phenomenon involving the engorgement of the clitoris”?

Clitoral erection: Physiological phenomenon involving the engorgement of the clitoris. Clitoral erection (also known as clitoral tumescence or female erection) is a physiological phenomenon where the clitoris becomes enlarged and firm.
One of the most intensively studied and intelligent cephalopods, this mollusk ranges from the Mediterranean and English coastline all the way to South Africa — which species?
Common octopus: Species of cephalopod. The common octopus (Octopus vulgaris) is a mollusk belonging to the class Cephalopoda.
These feather-gilled freshwater crustaceans share their taxonomic order with lobsters and turn up in everything from brooks to rice paddies — what are they?
Crayfish: Freshwater crustaceans. Crayfish are freshwater crustaceans belonging to the infraorder Astacidea, which also contains lobsters.
The first Western European combat aircraft to break Mach 2 in level flight, achieving the feat in October 1958, which French fighter jet family was this?
Dassault Mirage III: French supersonic fighter/interceptor aircraft.

Discovered in Arizona in the 1940s and first classified as a species of Megalosaurus, this theropod was reassigned to a new genus in 1970 once paleontologists noticed the twin crests on its skull — which dinosaur?
Dilophosaurus: Genus of theropod dinosaur from the Early Jurassic.

Coined by Robert Spitzer in the late 1970s to replace the notion of a "depressive personality," this condition resembles major depression but lingers for at least two years — and now goes by "persistent depressive disorder." What was its original name?
Dysthymia: Psychiatric disorder defined by chronic depression.
Caused by viruses like herpes simplex or rabies, this inflammation of the brain can bring fever, confusion, and a stiff neck — what is this condition?

Encephalitis: Inflammation of the brain. The severity can be variable with symptoms including reduction or alteration in consciousness, aphasia, headache, fever, confusion, a stiff neck, and vomiting.
This complex-analysis identity states that e raised to the power of ix equals cosine x plus i times sine x, linking exponential and trigonometric functions — what is it called?
Euler's formula: Complex exponential in terms of sine and cosine. The formula is still valid if x is a complex number, and is also called Euler's formula in this more general case.
Its 41 living species boast the most varied fur patterns of any land carnivore, all armed with retractile claws and an obligate taste for meat — which family is this?
Felidae: Family of mammals. Felidae ( FEE-lə-dee) is the family of mammals in the order Carnivora colloquially referred to as cats.

First described by 19th-century French psychiatrists Charles Lasègue and Jules Falret, this rare condition — also called shared psychotic disorder — lets one person's delusion spread to another. What is it called?

Folie à deux: Shared psychosis, a psychotic disorder. The disorder, first conceptualized in 19th century French psychiatry by Charles Lasègue and Jules Falret, is also known as Lasègue–Falret syndrome.
Sometimes called 'poor man's pepper' or 'pepper grass,' this fast-growing herb has a peppery bite similar to mustard — which plant?
Garden cress: Species of edible herb.

This general term covers any organ that secretes substances either straight into the bloodstream, like endocrine ones, or through a duct to a body surface, like exocrine ones — what type of structure is it?
Gland: Type of animal organ. A gland may also function to remove unwanted substances such as urine from the body.
Known to the British as the Martlet, this American carrier-based fighter entered service in 1940 and remained the U.S. Navy's best fighter against the Mitsubishi Zero until mid-1943 — which aircraft?
Grumman F4F Wildcat: United States Navy World War II era fighter plane.
This German physicist was the first to conclusively demonstrate the electromagnetic waves predicted by James Clerk Maxwell's equations — who is he?
Introduced in 1948 by a French naturalist, this taxonomic tribe groups humans together with chimpanzees and bonobos, but excludes gorillas — which tribe?
Hominini: Tribe of mammals. The Hominini (hominins) form a taxonomic tribe of the subfamily Homininae (hominines).

Responsible for nearly half a million deaths each year, this condition occurs when the body produces or absorbs more heat than it can dissipate, most often from heat stroke or a drug reaction — what condition?
Hyperthermia: Elevated body temperature due to failed thermoregulation.
This concept in calculus, a continuous analog of a sum, computes the signed area under a curve and pairs with differentiation as one of the field's two fundamental operations?
This fragrant genus of shrubs and vines in the olive family is grown in vast quantities in one Egyptian village that supplies much of the world's perfume industry — which plant?
Jasmine: Genus of flowering plant in the olive family Oleaceae.
Born Giulia Maddalena Angela in Italy, this physician became a leading freethinker and activist for women's rights and social reform in early-20th-century Argentina — who is she?
Julieta Lanteri: Argentine doctor and activist (1873–1932)

Ranked alongside Aristotle and Frege among history's most significant logicians, this thinker proved his completeness theorem in his 1929 Vienna dissertation before publishing his famous incompleteness theorems two years later — who is he?
Kurt Gödel: Mathematical logician and philosopher.
Marked by weariness and a desire to act without the energy to do so, which condition can be a normal response to poor sleep or stress, or a sign of underlying illness?
Lethargy: State of tiredness, weariness, fatigue, or lack of energy.
Reaching about 200 kg at its largest, this reddish-brown-shelled reptile ranges through the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans as well as the Mediterranean — which species?
Loggerhead sea turtle: Species of marine reptile distributed throughout the world.
A former mayor of Tehran and engineer by training, he served as Iran's sixth president from 2005 to 2013 and championed the country's nuclear program — who is he?

Mahmoud Ahmadinejad: President of Iran from 2005 to 2013. Mahmoud Ahmadinejad (né Sabbaghian; born 28 October 1956) is an Iranian politician who served as the sixth president of Iran from 2005 to 2013.

Born from a US-UK cooperative effort begun in the early 1970s to improve on a first-generation jump jet, this vertical-takeoff-capable attack aircraft has served the US Marine Corps plus Spanish and Italian navies — which aircraft?
McDonnell Douglas AV-8B Harrier II: Anglo-American VSTOL ground-attack aircraft.
Sold under brand names like Ritalin and Concerta, which stimulant medication is preferred as the first-line treatment for ADHD in children, while amphetamine is favored for adults?
Famous for mimicking the songs of other birds — and even singing well past midnight — this bird can recognize individual humans and is the state bird of five U.S. states. What kind of bird is it?
Mockingbird: Family of birds. The only mockingbird commonly found in North America is the northern mockingbird.
This autoimmune disease attacks acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction, often causing drooping eyelids, double vision, and difficulty swallowing — which condition?
Myasthenia gravis: Autoimmune disease resulting in skeletal muscle weakness.
This semiaquatic salamander's juvenile phase is nicknamed an 'eft,' and adults return to the water every year to breed after living mostly on land — what is it?
Newt: Salamander in the subfamily Pleurodelinae.
This medical condition, defined by a body mass index over 30, is linked to heart disease, type 2 diabetes and sleep apnea — what is it?
Obesity: Medical condition of excess body fat.
This fluid-filled sac that forms within the ovary is usually harmless and often tied to ovulation, appearing as a follicular or corpus luteum type — what is it?
Ovarian cyst: Fluid-filled sac in the ovary. If the cyst either breaks open or causes twisting of the ovary, it may cause severe pain.
Best known for creating Gmail, this engineer also built the first prototype of Google's ad platform and once suggested the company's old motto, 'Don't be evil' — who is he?
Known on the street as 'angel dust,' this dissociative anesthetic acts as an NMDA receptor antagonist and can cause hallucinations and psychosis — what is this drug?
Phencyclidine: Dissociative hallucinogenic drug, mostly used recreationally.
Native to Eurasia and temperate Africa but now naturalized worldwide, this flowering plant shares a common name with a banana-like fruit despite being unrelated to it — which species?
Plantago major: Species of flowering plant in the plantain family Plantaginaceae.
Covering the front part of the frontal lobe, this brain region orchestrates higher-order thinking including focus, decision-making, and impulse control — what is it?
Prefrontal cortex: Part of the brain responsible for personality, decision-making, and social behavior.
Emitting beams of radiation from its magnetic poles like a cosmic lighthouse, this highly magnetized, rapidly rotating neutron star produces remarkably precise, repeating pulses — what is it?
Pulsar: Type of neutron star with beams of radiation.

A canine native to the southeastern United States, intermediate in size between the coyote and gray wolf. For a century its status as a separate species has been debated — some call it a coywolf. Name this animal.
Red wolf: Canid native to the southeastern United States. Fish and Wildlife Service recognizes the red wolf as an endangered species and grants it protected status.
A Jesuit priest and polymath from the Republic of Ragusa produced an early precursor of atomic theory and, in 1753, discovered that the Moon has no atmosphere — who was he?
Roger Joseph Boscovich: Croat-Italian physicist and writer (1711–1787)
This Taiwanese-American physicist shared the 1976 Nobel Prize with Burton Richter for discovering the subatomic J/ψ particle. Who is he?
Samuel C. C. Ting: Nobel prize winning physicist.
The sole living species in its genus, this coastal California evergreen is the tallest tree species on Earth, reaching over 116 meters and living 2,200 years or more. What is it?
Sequoia sempervirens: Species of tree. Sequoia sempervirens is the sole living species of the genus Sequoia in the cypress family Cupressaceae (formerly treated in Taxodiaceae).

Its last natural case appeared in 1977, and in 1980 the WHO declared it the only human disease ever wiped off the Earth — which scourge, known for fluid-filled blisters that scarred survivors, was it?
Commonly nicknamed phlegm, this mucus coughed up from the trachea and bronchi is examined for tell-tale yellow or green coloring that signals infection — what is it?
Sputum: Mucus that is coughed up from the lower airways.

Serving under both Presidents Sukarno and Suharto, this Indonesian economist held posts across trade, finance, and research ministries, and once lobbied Washington against Dutch colonial rule — who was he?
Sumitro Djojohadikusumo: Indonesian statesman and economist (1917–2001)
The earliest known example was the stone tool, and the later control of fire is even credited with helping grow the human brain and spark language — what broad field is being described?
Technology: Use of knowledge for practical goals.
Tucked behind the breastbone and in front of the heart, this two-lobed organ is where immature T cells mature, and it's most active before adolescence — which organ?
Its name translates to 'three-horned face,' and this frilled dinosaur roamed present-day western North America right up until the asteroid strike 66 million years ago — what dinosaur is it?
